- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes, then corrects with a lag — model lags behind true trend reversals.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices return to prior averages too quickly, missing sustained momentum.
- Forecasts show higher variance than actuals, especially in the final 5–10 days — model overreacts to short-term noise.
- When true prices dip sharply, model fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates downside risk.
- Model often misjudges the timing of price peaks — tends to peak too early or too late relative to true market behavior.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days after a price spike, then gradually adjust — but too slowly to capture true momentum.
